The Heawood graph can be represented using LCF notation [5,-5]^7, which means starting with a 14-cycle and adding chords where each vertex connects to vertices at distance ±5 in an alternating pattern. So the Hamilton cycle gives me edges 0-1, 1-2, and so on around to 13-0, and then the chords add connections like 0-5, 1-10, 2-7, 3-12, and continuing this pattern through all 14 vertices. All the chord edges connect vertices from opposite partitions, confirming the graph is bipartite and therefore 2-colorable. The Heawood graph has a known girth of 6, and I can now list out all 21 edges: the 14 cycle edges plus the 7 chord edges connecting vertices according to the pattern.
